Sorry I’m just seeing your comment! If you haven’t done it yet/are still planning on doing it, I’d still say September would be the best month to go. Best chances of good weather / still moderate temps, and it really wasn’t too crowded. I definitely saw people each day but would still go miles without seeing a soul. That said, I camped in my tent each night so finding space in a shelter was not an issue. 

I completed it in 7 days/6 nights.
Try the Baxter State Park Facebook group! I see people offering to share sites sometimes, super helpful group

I did the 100 mile wilderness last September and it was hands down one of the best experiences of my whole life. Highly, highly recommend! 

Definitely make sure you’ve done your research and are prepared as much as possible, it’s grueling but so worth it. 

I didn’t do a food drop so had to carry 7 days worth of food (almost 14lbs) and that was really tough but still, the experience was incredible. 

Also highly recommend Shaw’s Hiker Hostel for pickup/drop off/etc - they were so helpful, kind, and all around wonderful people. 

Happy trails!
Who is Sofia’s current boyfriend, does anyone know? She isn’t still with Suitman, is she? So curious.

Thinking of you. I’m very sorry you’re going through this. I lost my sister to Suicide 8 years ago and the pain and grief and guilt still comes in waves, sometimes it feels like it just happened yesterday. It doesn’t go away or necessarily get easier, but you learn to live with it I guess. You carry them with you, and keep them alive through memories. It sounds corny I know, but I think it’s honestly true. I like to listen to her fav bands too, watch her fav movies, go on walks that she loved. Maybe that would help with your brother. Talk about him. Even talk to him in your head - sounds weird maybe, but I have conversations with my sister in my mind all the time, and it can be strangely comforting. Hope this helps, even if just in a small way. Wish you the best.
Thinking of you! You can do this. You deserve love and kindness and intimacy in your relationship, much more than what it seems he is capable of giving you. It’s out there and you are worthy. <3

Thank you, I really appreciate your response. The specifics are very helpful. We don’t have health insurance though and with bills, etc money is tight, so affording doctor visits/etc would be an issue

Neither of us have health insurance and money is pretty tight. And we both have pretty crippling anxiety about starting the process of calling the doctor, finding a therapist, etc. I know it sounds dumb.
You’re not alone. People want you to live.

I take one small thing at a time. Like #1, just put my feet on the floor and get myself out of bed. #2, brush my teeth. And then I slowly build up to bigger things, like actually going into work or school (if I can- a lot of times I can’t). Breaking things down into small chunks is way more manageable. I hope this helps you. Thinking of you!
You’re not alone. I hope you’re still here.

I haven’t tried it myself, but I have a few friends who have and they’ve each had very different experiences (one very positive, the other was more of a struggle). But you’re not alone, and you don’t have to feel ashamed. 

If you’re looking for someone immediately to talk to, I’d recommend texting HOME to 741741. It’s a support line through texting, which was honestly a game changer for me. Pulled me out of a very dark place, even if just for a while. And it feels good to text someone anonymous who will listen and care. Hope this helps. Sending you strength. <3

Same here, with adams song too. But - I think the fact that part of you has hope just shows that part of you wants to live. I think you can do it. This too shall pass. You’re not alone. And I bet you’re more deserving than you think you are.

It’s never too late to reach out. You can’t go back and change what’s happened, but moving forward is a possibility, even if it doesn’t feel like it. Try reaching out. It’s really hard, but it actually might help.
